official.deadline_central_display: 15 January 2027 (published by the Faculty of Science and the Amsterdam Law School for the September 2027 start)
official.deadline_note: There is no single central AMS deadline: the central page states 'Deadlines for the AMS differ per Faculty or Graduate School.' Published dates for the September 2027 start: Faculty of Science 15 January; Amsterdam Law School 15 January 23:59 CET with the full LLM application (outcome by end of March); Graduate School of Social Sciences 15 February 2027 23:59 CET, described as the final date with no late applications; the Psychology AMS page still shows the previous cycle's 1 March 2026 deadline.
official.application_cycle: 2027-2028 academic year (September 2027 start); awarded once a year to students starting in September
official.status_note: The Faculty of Science has published its September 2027 terms (one AMS of EUR 26,125, deadline 15 January) and the Amsterdam Law School confirms the 2027-2028 cycle, for which the scholarship amount is still 'to be announced'.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Faculty of Science: 'The scholarship cannot be used as a (partial) tuition fee waiver; the AMS recipient must still pay the full amount of tuition fee (with the possibility to pay this amount in monthly instalments).' Graduate School of Social Sciences: 'The scholarship equals the tuition fee. Please note that the scholarship cannot be used as a (partial) tuition waiver. The applicant must still pay the full amount of tuition due, and can do this in instalments.' Graduate School of Psychology: 'The AMS is a scholarship that covers part of the tuition fee.'
official.funding_period: per academic year, paid in monthly instalments
benefits: A cash grant of EUR 26,125 for the September 2027 start (Faculty of Science - the only faculty currently publishing a figure); the Amsterdam Law School's 2027-2028 amount is still to be announced
The grant is paid in monthly instalments

Second-year continuation for two-year master's programmes subject to study progress (Faculty of Science: at least 40 ECTS in the first year; Graduate School of Social Sciences: approximately 80% of credits per year)
eligibility: Hold a non-EU/EEA passport and have applied for a degree programme at the University of Amsterdam (the Faculty of Science also excludes Swiss nationality)
Not be eligible for support under the Dutch system of study grants and loans (Studiefinanciering) or for the reduced EEA tuition fee rate at the UvA
Not receive a full-coverage scholarship for the same period of study (Psychology: no other financial assistance providing substantial coverage)
Submit a complete application to an eligible UvA master's programme and be admitted for the first time; enrol as a full-time student for the academic year
Be able to comply with Dutch visa regulations

Have sufficient funds to cover all other costs (Faculty of Science additionally requires the previous academic programme to be completed no more than three years ago; the Graduate School of Social Sciences excludes pre-Master's candidates, except where only the summer-school methodology programme is required)
requirements: Indicate in the master's programme application that you wish to be considered for a UvA scholarship (Law: use the 'Scholarship' tab and select the AMS)
Submit the entire application before the faculty deadline (15 January at the Faculty of Science and the Amsterdam Law School; 15 February 2027 at the Graduate School of Social Sciences)

Upload the faculty's scholarship documents: a motivation letter of maximum 500 words (Faculties of Science and Law) or a single self-composed PDF containing CV, motivation letter, letter of recommendation and financial plan (Graduate School of Social Sciences)

Be fully and unconditionally admitted to the eligible programme (Psychology requires unconditional acceptance; the Graduate School of Social Sciences requires the programme to be the applicant's first programme in the Netherlands)
Notify the scholarship office of any change in nationality, type of residence permit or additional financial support during the academic year
documents: Motivation letter, maximum 500 words, explaining the choice of programme and the relevance of the scholarship (Faculties of Science and Law)
Curriculum vitae (Faculties of Science and Social Sciences)
Letter of recommendation written by a professor or another member of academic staff, indicating academic qualities (Graduate School of Social Sciences)
Financial plan showing that you need the scholarship and have sufficient funds to cover all other costs (Graduate School of Social Sciences)
selection_criteria: Academic records: Faculty of Science expects the top 10% of graduates from the class (GPA 3.5 on the US 4-point scale, first class honours/upper division UK, or 8+ on the Dutch 10-point scale); Amsterdam Law School requires a GPA comparable to 4.0 (USA), first class honours (UK) or 8.0 (Dutch), counting only law courses for non-legal bachelors
Academic quality of the institute where the previous degree was obtained (Faculty of Science)
Quality of the motivation letter (maximum 500 words) explaining the reasons for choosing the programme and the relevance of the scholarship for the future academic career
Curriculum vitae including extracurricular activities such as student commissions, international experience, high-level sports or music, or volunteer work (Faculty of Science)

Academic excellence and promise evidenced by academic records and a letter of recommendation (Graduate School of Social Sciences); former academic performance and sufficient English language skills (Graduate School of Psychology)
At the Amsterdam Law School the AMS is awarded through a lottery system, randomly selecting from applicants who meet the requirements
coverage: Cash merit grant of EUR 26,125 for the September 2027 start (Faculty of Science); the Graduate School of Social Sciences states the scholarship 'equals the tuition fee' and Psychology that it 'covers part of the tuition fee'
Paid to the recipient in monthly instalments
Cannot be used as a (partial) tuition fee waiver - the recipient must still pay the full tuition fee, which the UvA allows to be paid in monthly instalments
No published housing, living-cost, insurance or travel allowance; applicants must document sufficient funds for all other costs
application_method: Submit a complete application to the eligible UvA master's programme (admission procedure of the programme)
In the application form answer 'yes' to the question whether you want to be considered for a UvA scholarship / select the AMS on the 'Scholarship' tab

Upload the faculty's scholarship documents in the 'Additional documents' section of the application system (Graduate School of Social Sciences: one PDF named 'scholarship application' uploaded under 'scholarship motivation letter')

The Admissions Office of the faculty/Graduate School assesses the scholarship application; failing to complete any step renders the scholarship application incomplete and it will not be taken into consideration
official.application_route: Apply through the master's programme application: tick the UvA scholarship question and upload the faculty's required documents - there is no separate AMS application form.
official.study_mode: full-time (enrolment as a full-time student for the academic year is required)
official.citizenship_residency: Must hold a non-EU/EEA passport (the Faculty of Science also excludes Swiss nationality); must not be eligible for Studiefinanciering or the reduced EEA tuition fee rate, and must be able to comply with Dutch visa regulations.
official.international_eligibility: Exclusively for students from outside the EU/EEA; the central page states that outstanding students from outside the EU/EEA can apply for an Amsterdam Merit Scholarship.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Must apply to an eligible master's programme at the faculty awarding the AMS: the Faculty of Science limits the award to its MSc programmes, the Amsterdam Law School to four LLM tracks (International and European Law; Transnational and European Private Law; Law & Finance; International Criminal Law), the Graduate School of Social Sciences to its English-taught selective master's programmes, and the Graduate School of Psychology to its one-year Master's or Research Master's in Psychology.
official.duration: One academic year per award; two-year master's recipients can receive the scholarship for the second year as well subject to study progress (Faculty of Science: at least 40 ECTS in the first year, plus satisfactory effort and progress).
official.description: The University of Amsterdam (UvA) aims to attract the world's brightest students to its international classrooms: outstanding students from outside the EU/EEA can apply for an Amsterdam Merit Scholarship. The AMS is awarded per faculty or Graduate School, so the amount, number of awards, deadlines, eligibility requirements and selection criteria differ per faculty, and applications are submitted to the Admissions Offices of the Graduate Schools as part of the master's programme application.
official.program_type: University merit scholarship for non-EU/EEA master's students, awarded per faculty or Graduate School
official.english_requirement: The central AMS page sets no English requirement; each master's programme sets its own language criteria. Published for the Graduate School of Psychology (same criteria as for admission to its master's tracks): IELTS academic at least 7.0 with a minimum of 6.5 per component, TOEFL iBT at least 100 (Reading 24, Listening 22, Speaking 25, Writing 24), or Cambridge C1 Advanced at least 190; test results may not be older than 2 years.

not_confirmed: A single university-wide AMS amount or award count - amounts and numbers are set per faculty; the Amsterdam Law School states the 2027-2028 amount is 'to be announced' and Humanities, Economics and Business, Medicine, Communication Science and Child Development and Education were not individually checked for the 2027-2028 cycle
Graduate School of Psychology deadline for the September 2027 start - its page still shows the previous cycle's 1 March 2026 deadline
An English language requirement for the AMS itself - none is set centrally; requirements come from each master's programme
Living-cost, housing, insurance or travel allowances - no faculty page publishes any
verification.notes: Checked the central AMS page and four faculty AMS pages (Science, Law, Social Sciences, Psychology) plus the UvA tuition-fee page on uva.nl; the EUR 26,125 figure and 15 January deadline come from the Faculty of Science page for the September 2027 start.

applicant_utility.summary: The AMS is not one scholarship but a family of small faculty-level awards for non-EU/EEA master's applicants, and only the Faculty of Science has published a figure for the 2027-2028 cycle (EUR 26,125, paid in monthly instalments). You apply by ticking the scholarship box inside your master's programme application, so an AMS request is only valid if the programme application itself is complete and submitted in the same round. Because the grant cannot be deducted from your tuition bill, treat it as cash support on top of a full non-EEA tuition fee plus roughly EUR 1,000-1,500 a month of Amsterdam living costs.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-decile non-EU/EEA graduates applying to a UvA master's who can independently fund tuition and living costs and want a modest monthly stipend on top.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify which faculty or Graduate School runs your programme and read its AMS page first - eligibility, documents and deadlines are set there, not centrally.

Confirm your passport and funding status against the nationality rules: non-EU/EEA (Swiss also excluded at the Faculty of Science), no entitlement to Studiefinanciering and no eligibility for the reduced EEA tuition rate.

Draft the 500-word motivation letter explaining why you chose the programme and why the scholarship matters for your future academic career - it is a selection criterion at every faculty that publishes one.

For the Graduate School of Social Sciences, assemble the single PDF (CV, motivation letter, recommendation letter, financial plan) well before 15 February 2027, and for the Amsterdam Law School remember both the 'Scholarship' tab selection and the letter upload are needed.

Budget for the full non-EEA institutional tuition (for example EUR 26,000 per year for a two-year Faculty of Science MSc in 2026-2027) plus EUR 1,000-1,500 monthly living costs; the AMS pays out monthly and cannot be offset against tuition.
Check how your faculty selects: a lottery among eligible applicants at the Amsterdam Law School versus merit ranking elsewhere, which changes where your effort should go.
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete scholarship submission: at the Amsterdam Law School you must both select the scholarship on the 'Scholarship' tab and upload the motivation letter, otherwise the application is not taken into consideration.
Nationality or funding-status mismatch: an EU/EEA passport, Swiss nationality at the Faculty of Science, eligibility for Studiefinanciering or the reduced EEA rate automatically disqualifies you.
Conditional or pre-Master's routes: the Graduate School of Social Sciences excludes pre-Master's candidates and requires unconditional admission, and Psychology requires unconditional acceptance.
Already holding a UvA master's degree (excluded by the Amsterdam Law School) or holding another full-coverage scholarship for the same study period.

An unpairable application: the Graduate School of Social Sciences invalidates a scholarship application that is not accompanied by a timely study-programme application, and its 15 February deadline is final with no late submissions.
A stale English test: at Psychology the IELTS, TOEFL or C1 Advanced result must be less than two years old, and high scores are themselves a selection criterion.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Full non-EEA institutional tuition (EUR 26,000 per year for a two-year Faculty of Science MSc and EUR 25,900 for one-year law or humanities master's at the 2026-2027 rates, set per academic year and indexed annually) plus Amsterdam living costs of roughly EUR 1,000-1,500 per month for housing, food, transport and health insurance, visa and residence-permit costs, and any pre-master's or summer-school costs; the AMS is a cash grant and nothing in it is earmarked for travel.
document_audit: Motivation letters are capped at 500 words at the Faculties of Science and Law; write to the limit, not beyond it.

The Graduate School of Social Sciences wants one self-composed PDF with all four documents in a row, uploaded under 'scholarship motivation letter' in 'Additional documents' - separate uploads miss the published instruction.
The recommendation letter for Social Sciences must come from a professor or academic staff member and speak to your academic qualities, not your character in general.
The Social Sciences financial plan must demonstrate both need for the scholarship and sufficient funds for all other costs - a bare bank statement does neither.
The Faculty of Science also weighs the CV including extracurricular activities, so a bare academic CV wastes a published selection criterion.
The Psychology Graduate School asks for no further scholarship documents beyond answering 'yes' in the application system - extra uploads there are not required.
alerts: Deadlines are faculty-specific for the September 2027 start: 15 January (Faculty of Science and Amsterdam Law School) and 15 February 2027 (Graduate School of Social Sciences); the Psychology page still lists 1 March 2026, so re-check it before relying on that date.
Selection runs in March with outcomes by end of March (Law), April (Science) or mid-May (Social Sciences) - do not wait for the result before arranging financing.

Award volumes are tiny: one AMS at the Faculty of Science, one at the Amsterdam Law School, two at the Graduate School of Social Sciences (1.5% of the 2025 applicants) and one each for the Psychology master's and research master's tracks.
At the Amsterdam Law School the award is a lottery among applicants who meet the requirements, so eligibility screening matters more than being top-ranked.
Holding another full-coverage scholarship disqualifies you, and you must notify the scholarship office of any change in nationality, residence permit or funding during the year.
Second-year continuation on two-year programmes is conditional on progress (at least 40 ECTS in year one at Science; approximately 80% of credits per year at Social Sciences).
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: The scholarship is requested inside the master's programme application in SIS: tick the UvA scholarship question, upload the faculty-specific documents, and the Admissions Office of your Graduate School screens and decides alongside the admission decision, notifying you between end of March and mid-May.
